questions.subject: science-and-technology
questions.question: Artificial way of causing rainfall to reduce air pollution makes use of
questions.explanation:
Artificial rainfall (cloud seeding) to reduce air pollution uses silver iodide and potassium iodide as seeding agents.

Silver iodide: The primary cloud seeding agent that acts as ice nuclei, helping water droplets in clouds to freeze and form precipitation. Its crystal structure is similar to ice, making it highly effective for inducing rainfall.

Potassium iodide: Used as a supplementary seeding agent that enhances the cloud seeding process and helps in the formation of precipitation.

This technique is used to wash out pollutants from the atmosphere, particularly during severe air pollution episodes. The induced rainfall helps bring down suspended particulate matter and other air pollutants, providing temporary relief from poor air quality conditions.

questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.question:
Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India :
I. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review.
II. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about Presidential pardoning power:

I. Exercise of this power can be subjected to limited judicial review: Correct. While the President's pardoning power is wide, the Supreme Court has held that it can be subject to judicial review on limited grounds such as whether the power was exercised malafide, based on irrelevant considerations, or in violation of constitutional principles.

II. President can exercise this power without advice of Central Government: Incorrect. The President exercises pardoning power on the advice of the Central Government (Council of Ministers). Like other executive powers, this is not exercised independently by the President but on ministerial advice as per the constitutional framework.

questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.question:
Consider the following statements :
I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately.
III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about the Speaker of Lok Sabha:

I. Speaker shall not vacate office until immediately before first meeting after dissolution: Correct. Article 94 provides that the Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly constituted House after general elections.

II. Member elected as Speaker must resign from political party immediately: Incorrect. There is no constitutional requirement for the Speaker to resign from their political party. While convention expects political neutrality, formal party resignation is not mandated.

III. Speaker may be removed by resolution with fourteen days' notice: Correct. Article 94 specifies that the Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all members, provided at least fourteen days' notice is given before moving such resolution.

questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.question:
Consider the following statements :
I. If any question arises as to whether a Member of the House of the People has become subject to disqualification under the 10th Schedule, the President's decision in accordance with the opinion of the Council of Union Ministers shall be final.
II. There is no mention of the word 'political party' in the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Under the 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), the decision on disqualification of a Member of the House of the People is made by the Speaker of the House, not the President. The President's role in disqualification matters is limited to cases under Articles 102/191, where the Election Commission's opinion is sought.

Statement II is incorrect. The word 'political party' is explicitly mentioned in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.

Both statements are incorrect.

questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I: In India, State Governments have no power for making rules for grant of concessions in respect of extraction of minor minerals even though such minerals are located in their territories.
Statement II: In India, the Central Government has the power to notify minor minerals under the relevant law.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct

questions.explanation:
Statement I: Incorrect. State Governments do have significant powers in making rules for grant of concessions regarding extraction of minor minerals. Under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, states have substantial authority over minor minerals found in their territories.

Statement II: Correct. The Central Government does have the power to notify and declare what constitutes 'minor minerals' under the relevant mining laws. This classification power helps define the scope of state versus central jurisdiction over different types of minerals.

questions.subject: polity-and-governance
questions.question: Which organization has enacted the Nature Restoration Law (NRL) to tackle climate change and biodiversity loss?

options.text: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development

questions.explanation:
The European Union (EU) has enacted the Nature Restoration Law (NRL) to tackle climate change and biodiversity loss.

The EU Nature Restoration Law is a comprehensive regulation aimed at restoring degraded ecosystems across the European Union. It sets legally binding targets for ecosystem restoration and biodiversity recovery, requiring member states to implement restoration measures for various habitats including forests, agricultural areas, marine ecosystems, and urban spaces.

This law is part of the EU's broader Green Deal strategy and represents one of the most ambitious environmental restoration initiatives globally, addressing both climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation through ecosystem restoration.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements :
I. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States.
II. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years.
III. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels and to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes and duties, leviable by the State, between the State and Panchayats at the intermediate level.
Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.explanation:
All three statements about intermediate level Panchayats are incorrect:

I. Panchayats at intermediate level exist in all States: Incorrect. Not all states have intermediate level (block/mandal) panchayats. States with population below 20 lakh are not required to have intermediate panchayats as per the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.

II. Minimum age for membership is thirty years: Incorrect. The minimum age for membership in panchayats at intermediate level is 25 years, not 30 years, as specified in the Constitution.

III. Chief Minister constitutes commission for financial review: Incorrect. It is the Governor, not the Chief Minister, who constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of panchayats and make recommendations for fund distribution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in respect of BIMSTEC :
I. It is a regional organization consisting of seven member States till January 2025.
II. It came into existence with the signing of the Dhaka Declaration, 1999.
III. Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Nepal are founding member States of BIMSTEC.
IV. In BIMSTEC, the subsector of 'tourism' is being led by India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about BIMSTEC:

I. Correct. BIMSTEC has seven member states as of January 2025: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.

II. Incorrect. BIMSTEC was established with the Bangkok Declaration in June 1997, not the Dhaka Declaration in 1999. It was originally called BIST-EC with four founding members.

III. Incorrect. The founding members of BIMSTEC (originally BIST-EC) in 1997 were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand. Myanmar joined later in 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004. So Nepal is not a founding member.

IV. Incorrect. According to the official BIMSTEC website, the tourism sub-sector falls under the "People-to-People Contact" sector, which is led by Nepal, not India. India leads the Security sector in BIMSTEC.

Therefore, only Statement I is correct.

questions.question:
GPS-Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) uses a system of ground stations to provide necessary augmentation. Which of the following statements is/are correct in respect of GAGAN?
I. It is designed to provide additional accuracy and integrity.
II. It will allow more uniform and high quality air traffic management.
III. It will provide benefits only in aviation but not in other modes of transportation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about GPS-Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN):

I. Designed to provide additional accuracy and integrity: Correct. GAGAN is a satellite-based augmentation system that enhances the accuracy and integrity of GPS signals for safety-critical navigation applications.

II. Will allow more uniform and high quality air traffic management: Correct. GAGAN enables precision approach procedures at airports, improving air traffic management efficiency and safety across Indian airspace with consistent navigation standards.

III. Provides benefits only in aviation, not other transportation modes: Incorrect. While GAGAN is primarily designed for aviation, its enhanced GPS accuracy and integrity can benefit other transportation modes including maritime, rail, and road transport applications requiring precise navigation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Lokpal:
I. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India.
II. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a Member of the Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory, and only the Chief Justice of India, whether incumbent or retired, has to be its Chairperson.
III. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as the Chairperson or Member, as the case may be.
IV. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.text: None of the above statements is correct

questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about Lokpal:

I. Power applies to public servants in India but not those posted outside: Incorrect. Lokpal's jurisdiction extends to public servants serving abroad in Indian missions and establishments.

II. Only Chief Justice of India can be Chairperson: Incorrect. While the CJI can be Chairperson, other qualified persons including former CJI, Supreme Court judges, or eminent persons can also be appointed as Chairperson.

III. Minimum age is forty-five years: Correct. The Lokpal Act specifies that the Chairperson or Member must be at least 45 years of age on the date of assuming office.

IV. Cannot inquire into allegations against sitting Prime Minister: Incorrect. Lokpal can inquire into corruption allegations against a sitting Prime Minister, though there are specific procedural safeguards for such investigations.

II. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world's youngest ever Grandmaster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Analyzing statements about chess achievements:

I. Gukesh became youngest winner in 45th Chess Olympiad 2024 by defeating Ian Nepomniachtchi: Incorrect. This statement confuses different chess competitions. Gukesh became the youngest World Chess Champion by winning the World Championship, not the Chess Olympiad. The Olympiad is a team event, not an individual championship.

II. Abhimanyu Mishra holds the record as world's youngest Grandmaster: Correct. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player of Indian origin, became the youngest chess Grandmaster in history when he achieved the title at the age of 12 years, 4 months, and 25 days in 2021.
